metric.label: Lexical baseline
metric.description: Character n-gram cosine distance. This is a reproducible lexical baseline, not a semantic or faithfulness score.

units.leftText: In the eighth month of the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to the prophet Zechariah son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo, saying:
units.rightText: In the eighth month, in the second year of Darius, came the word of Jehovah unto Zechariah the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo, the prophet, saying,

units.leftText: “The LORD was very angry with your fathers.
units.rightText: Jehovah was sore displeased with your fathers.

units.leftText: So tell the people that this is what the LORD of Hosts says: ‘Return to Me, declares the LORD of Hosts, and I will return to you, says the LORD of Hosts.’
units.rightText: Therefore say thou unto them, Thus saith Jehovah of hosts: Return unto me, saith Jehovah of hosts, and I will return unto you, saith Jehovah of hosts.

units.leftText: Do not be like your fathers, to whom the former prophets proclaimed that this is what the LORD of Hosts says: ‘Turn now from your evil ways and deeds.’ But they did not listen or pay attention to Me, declares the LORD.
units.rightText: Be ye not as your fathers, unto whom the former prophets cried, saying, Thus saith Jehovah of hosts, Return ye now from your evil ways, and from your evil doings: but they did not hear, nor hearken unto me, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: Where are your fathers now? And the prophets, do they live forever?
units.rightText: Your fathers, where are they? and the prophets, do they live for ever?

units.leftText: But did not My words and My statutes, which I commanded My servants the prophets, overtake your fathers? They repented and said, ‘Just as the LORD of Hosts purposed to do to us according to our ways and deeds, so He has done to us.’” The Vision of the Horses
units.rightText: But my words and my statutes, which I commanded my servants the prophets, did they not overtake your fathers? and they turned and said, Like as Jehovah of hosts thought to do unto us, according to our ways, and according to our doings, so hath he dealt with us.

units.leftText: On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, the month of Shebat, in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to the prophet Zechariah son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo.
units.rightText: Upon the four and twentieth day of the eleventh month, which is the month Shebat, in the second year of Darius, came the word of Jehovah unto Zechariah the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo, the prophet, saying,
leftNotes: 1:7 Shebat is the eleventh month of the Hebrew lunar calendar, usually occurring within the months of January and February.

units.leftText: I looked out into the night and saw a man riding on a red horse. He was standing among the myrtle trees in the hollow, and behind him were red, sorrel, and white horses.
units.rightText: I saw in the night, and, behold, a man riding upon a red horse, and he stood among the myrtle-trees that were in the bottom; and behind him there were horses, red, sorrel, and white.

units.leftText: “What are these, my lord?” I asked. And the angel who was speaking with me replied, “I will show you what they are.”
units.rightText: Then said I, O my lord, what are these? And the angel that talked with me said unto me, I will show thee what these are.

units.leftText: Then the man standing among the myrtle trees explained, “They are the ones the LORD has sent to patrol the earth.”
units.rightText: And the man that stood among the myrtle-trees answered and said, These are they whom Jehovah hath sent to walk to and fro through the earth.

units.leftText: And the riders answered the angel of the LORD who was standing among the myrtle trees, “We have patrolled the earth, and behold, all the earth is at rest and tranquil.”
units.rightText: And they answered the angel of Jehovah that stood among the myrtle-trees, and said, We have walked to and fro through the earth, and, behold, all the earth sitteth still, and is at rest.

units.leftText: Then the angel of the LORD said, “How long, O LORD of Hosts, will You withhold mercy from Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, with which You have been angry these seventy years?”
units.rightText: Then the angel of Jehovah answered and said, O Jehovah of hosts, how long wilt thou not have mercy on Jerusalem and on the cities of Judah, against which thou hast had indignation these threescore and ten years?

units.leftText: So the LORD spoke kind and comforting words to the angel who was speaking with me.
units.rightText: And Jehovah answered the angel that talked with me with good words, even comfortable words.

units.leftText: Then the angel who was speaking with me said, “Proclaim this word: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: ‘I am very jealous for Jerusalem and Zion,
units.rightText: So the angel that talked with me said unto me, Cry thou, saying, Thus saith Jehovah of hosts: I am jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion with a great jealousy.

units.leftText: but I am fiercely angry with the nations that are at ease. For I was a little angry, but they have added to the calamity. ’
units.rightText: And I am very sore displeased with the nations that are at ease; for I was but a little displeased, and they helped forward the affliction.
leftNotes: 1:15 Or they have overdone the punishment

units.leftText: Therefore this is what the LORD says: ‘I will return to Jerusalem with mercy, and there My house will be rebuilt, declares the LORD of Hosts, and a measuring line will be stretched out over Jerusalem.’
units.rightText: Therefore thus saith Jehovah: I am returned to Jerusalem with mercies; my house shall be built in it, saith Jehovah of hosts, and a line shall be stretched forth over Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Proclaim further that this is what the LORD of Hosts says: ‘My cities will again overflow with prosperity; the LORD will again comfort Zion and choose Jerusalem.’” The Vision of the Horns and the Craftsmen
units.rightText: Cry yet again, saying, Thus saith Jehovah of hosts: My cities shall yet overflow with prosperity; and Jehovah shall yet comfort Zion, and shall yet choose Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Then I looked up and saw four horns.
units.rightText: And I lifted up mine eyes, and saw, and, behold, four horns.

units.leftText: So I asked the angel who was speaking with me, “What are these?” And he told me, “These are the horns that have scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem.”
units.rightText: And I said unto the angel that talked with me, What are these? And he answered me, These are the horns which have scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Then the LORD showed me four craftsmen.
units.rightText: And Jehovah showed me four smiths.

units.leftText: “What are these coming to do?” I asked. And He replied, “These are the horns that scattered Judah so that no one could raise his head; but the craftsmen have come to terrify them and throw down these horns of the nations that have lifted up their horns against the land of Judah to scatter it.”
units.rightText: Then said I, What come these to do? And he spake, saying, These are the horns which scattered Judah, so that no man did lift up his head; but these are come to terrify them, to cast down the horns of the nations, which lifted up their horn against the land of Judah to scatter it.

units.leftText: Then I lifted up my eyes and saw a man with a measuring line in his hand.
units.rightText: And I lifted up mine eyes, and saw, and, behold, a man with a measuring line in his hand.

units.leftText: “Where are you going?” I asked. “To measure Jerusalem,” he replied, “and to determine its width and length.”
units.rightText: Then said I, Whither goest thou? And he said unto me, To measure Jerusalem, to see what is the breadth thereof, and what is the length thereof.

units.leftText: Then the angel who was speaking with me went forth, and another angel came forward to meet him
units.rightText: And, behold, the angel that talked with me went forth, and another angel went out to meet him,

units.leftText: and said to him, “Run and tell that young man: ‘Jerusalem will be a city without walls because of the multitude of men and livestock within it.
units.rightText: and said unto him, Run, speak to this young man, saying, Jerusalem shall be inhabited as villages without walls, by reason of the multitude of men and cattle therein.

units.leftText: For I will be a wall of fire around it, declares the LORD, and I will be the glory within it.’” The Redemption of Zion (Hosea 3:1–5|HOS 3:1-5*)
units.rightText: For I, saith Jehovah, will be unto her a wall of fire round about, and I will be the glory in the midst of her.

units.leftText: “Get up! Get up! Flee from the land of the north,” declares the LORD, “for I have scattered you like the four winds of heaven,” declares the LORD.
units.rightText: Ho, ho, flee from the land of the north, saith Jehovah; for I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heavens, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: “Get up, O Zion! Escape, you who dwell with the Daughter of Babylon!”
units.rightText: Ho Zion, escape, thou that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.

units.leftText: For this is what the LORD of Hosts says: “After His Glory has sent Me against the nations that have plundered you — for whoever touches you touches the apple of His eye —
units.rightText: For thus saith Jehovah of hosts: After glory hath he sent me unto the nations which plundered you; for he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye.
leftNotes: 2:8 Or After the Glorious One has sent Me or After He has honored Me and sent Me
2:8 Or the pupil

units.leftText: I will surely wave My hand over them, so that they will become plunder for their own servants. Then you will know that the LORD of Hosts has sent Me.”
units.rightText: For, behold, I will shake my hand over them, and they shall be a spoil to those that served them; and ye shall know that Jehovah of hosts hath sent me.

units.leftText: “Shout for joy and be glad, O Daughter of Zion, for I am coming to dwell among you,” declares the LORD.
units.rightText: Sing and rejoice, O daughter of Zion; for, lo, I come, and I will dwell in the midst of thee, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: “On that day many nations will join themselves to the LORD, and they will become My people. I will dwell among you, and you will know that the LORD of Hosts has sent Me to you.
units.rightText: And many nations shall join themselves to Jehovah in that day, and shall be my people; and I will dwell in the midst of thee, and thou shalt know that Jehovah of hosts hath sent me unto thee.

units.leftText: And the LORD will take possession of Judah as His portion in the Holy Land, and He will once again choose Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And Jehovah shall inherit Judah as his portion in the holy land, and shall yet choose Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Be silent before the LORD, all people, for He has roused Himself from His holy dwelling.”
units.rightText: Be silent, all flesh, before Jehovah; for he is waked up out of his holy habitation.

units.leftText: Then the angel showed me Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of the LORD, with Satan standing at his right hand to accuse him.
units.rightText: And he showed me Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of Jehovah, and Satan standing at his right hand to be his adversary.
leftNotes: 3:1 Or Angel; also in verses 3, 4, 5, and 6; corresponding pronouns may also be capitalized.
3:1 That is, the Accuser or the Adversary; also in verse 2

units.leftText: And the LORD said to Satan: “The LORD rebukes you, Satan! Indeed, the LORD, who has chosen Jerusalem, rebukes you! Is not this man a firebrand snatched from the fire?”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Satan, Jehovah rebuke thee, O Satan; yea, Jehovah that hath chosen Jerusalem rebuke thee: is not this a brand plucked out of the fire?
leftNotes: 3:2 That is, a burning stick

units.leftText: Now Joshua was dressed in filthy garments as he stood before the angel.
units.rightText: Now Joshua was clothed with filthy garments, and was standing before the angel.

units.leftText: So the angel said to those standing before him, “Take off his filthy clothes!” Then he said to Joshua, “See, I have removed your iniquity, and I will clothe you with splendid robes.”
units.rightText: And he answered and spake unto those that stood before him, saying, Take the filthy garments from off him. And unto him he said, Behold, I have caused thine iniquity to pass from thee, and I will clothe thee with rich apparel.

units.leftText: Then I said, “Let them put a clean turban on his head.” So a clean turban was placed on his head, and they clothed him, as the angel of the LORD stood by.
units.rightText: And I said, Let them set a clean mitre upon his head. So they set a clean mitre upon his head, and clothed him with garments; and the angel of Jehovah was standing by.

units.leftText: Then the angel of the LORD gave this charge to Joshua:
units.rightText: And the angel of Jehovah protested unto Joshua, saying,

units.leftText: “This is what the LORD of Hosts says: ‘If you walk in My ways and keep My instructions, then you will govern My house and will also have charge of My courts; and I will give you a place among these who are standing here.
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah of hosts: If thou wilt walk in my ways, and if thou wilt keep my charge, then thou also shalt judge my house, and shalt also keep my courts, and I will give thee a place of access among these that stand by.

units.leftText: Hear now, O high priest Joshua, you and your companions seated before you, who are indeed a sign. For behold, I am going to bring My servant, the Branch.
units.rightText: Hear now, O Joshua the high priest, thou and thy fellows that sit before thee; for they are men that are a sign: for, behold, I will bring forth my servant the Branch.

units.leftText: See the stone I have set before Joshua; on that one stone are seven eyes. Behold, I will engrave on it an inscription, declares the LORD of Hosts, and I will remove the iniquity of this land in a single day.
units.rightText: For, behold, the stone that I have set before Joshua; upon one stone are seven eyes: behold, I will engrave the graving thereof, saith Jehovah of hosts, and I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day.
leftNotes: 3:9 Or facets

units.leftText: On that day, declares the LORD of Hosts, you will each invite your neighbor to sit under your own vine and fig tree.’”
units.rightText: In that day, saith Jehovah of hosts, shall ye invite every man his neighbor under the vine and under the fig-tree.

units.leftText: Then the angel who was speaking with me returned and woke me, as a man is awakened from his sleep.
units.rightText: And the angel that talked with me came again, and waked me, as a man that is wakened out of his sleep.

units.leftText: “What do you see?” he asked.
units.rightText: And he said unto me, What seest thou? And I said, I have seen, and, behold, a candlestick all of gold, with its bowl upon the top of it, and its seven lamps thereon; there are seven pipes to each of the lamps, which are upon the top thereof;

units.leftText: There are also two olive trees beside it, one on the right side of the bowl and the other on its left.”
units.rightText: and two olive-trees by it, one upon the right side of the bowl, and the other upon the left side thereof.

units.leftText: “What are these, my lord?” I asked the angel who was speaking with me.
units.rightText: And I answered and spake to the angel that talked with me, saying, What are these, my lord?

units.leftText: “Do you not know what they are?” replied the angel. “No, my lord,” I answered.
units.rightText: Then the angel that talked with me answered and said unto me, Knowest thou not what these are? And I said, No, my lord.

units.leftText: So he said to me, “This is the word of the LORD to Zerubbabel: Not by might nor by power, but by My Spirit, says the LORD of Hosts.
units.rightText: Then he answered and spake unto me, saying, This is the word of Jehovah unto Zerubbabel, saying, Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit, saith Jehovah of hosts.

units.leftText: What are you, O great mountain? Before Zerubbabel you will become a plain. Then he will bring forth the capstone accompanied by shouts of ‘Grace, grace to it!’”
units.rightText: Who art thou, O great mountain? before Zerubbabel thou shalt become a plain; and he shall bring forth the top stone with shoutings of Grace, grace, unto it.

units.leftText: Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
units.rightText: Moreover the word of Jehovah came unto me, saying,

units.leftText: “The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house, and his hands will complete it. Then you will know that the LORD of Hosts has sent me to you.
units.rightText: The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house; his hands shall also finish it; and thou shalt know that Jehovah of hosts hath sent me unto you.

units.leftText: For who has despised the day of small things? But these seven eyes of the LORD, which scan the whole earth, will rejoice when they see the plumb line in the hand of Zerubbabel.”
units.rightText: For who hath despised the day of small things? for these seven shall rejoice, and shall see the plummet in the hand of Zerubbabel; these are the eyes of Jehovah, which run to and fro through the whole earth.
leftNotes: 4:10 Or facets
4:10 Or the chosen capstone

units.leftText: Then I asked the angel, “What are the two olive trees on the right and left of the lampstand?”
units.rightText: Then answered I, and said unto him, What are these two olive-trees upon the right side of the candlestick and upon the left side thereof?

units.leftText: And I questioned him further, “What are the two olive branches beside the two gold pipes from which the golden oil pours?”
units.rightText: And I answered the second time, and said unto him, What are these two olive-branches, which are beside the two golden spouts, that empty the golden oil out of themselves?
leftNotes: 4:12 Hebrew from which the gold

units.leftText: “Do you not know what these are?” he inquired. “No, my lord,” I replied.
units.rightText: And he answered me and said, Knowest thou not what these are? And I said, No, my lord.

units.leftText: So he said, “These are the two anointed ones who are standing beside the Lord of all the earth.”
units.rightText: Then said he, These are the two anointed ones, that stand by the Lord of the whole earth.
leftNotes: 4:14 Hebrew the two sons of new oil
4:14 See Revelation 11:4|REV 11:4*.

units.leftText: Again I lifted up my eyes and saw before me a flying scroll.
units.rightText: Then again I lifted up mine eyes, and saw, and, behold, a flying roll.

units.leftText: “What do you see?” asked the angel. “I see a flying scroll,” I replied, “twenty cubits long and ten cubits wide. ”
units.rightText: And he said unto me, What seest thou? And I answered, I see a flying roll; the length thereof is twenty cubits, and the breadth thereof ten cubits.
leftNotes: 5:2 The flying scroll was approximately 30 feet long and 15 feet wide (9.1 meters long and 4.6 meters wide).

units.leftText: Then he told me, “This is the curse that is going out over the face of all the land, for according to one side of the scroll, every thief will be removed; and according to the other side, every perjurer will be removed.
units.rightText: Then said he unto me, This is the curse that goeth forth over the face of the whole land: for every one that stealeth shall be cut off on the one side according to it; and every one that sweareth shall be cut off on the other side according to it.

units.leftText: I will send it out, declares the LORD of Hosts, and it will enter the house of the thief and the house of him who swears falsely by My name. It will remain inside his house and destroy it, down to its timbers and stones.” The Vision of the Woman in a Basket
units.rightText: I will cause it to go forth, saith Jehovah of hosts, and it shall enter into the house of the thief, and into the house of him that sweareth falsely by my name; and it shall abide in the midst of his house, and shall consume it with the timber thereof and the stones thereof.

units.leftText: Then the angel who was speaking with me came forward and told me, “Now lift up your eyes and see what is approaching.”
units.rightText: Then the angel that talked with me went forth, and said unto me, Lift up now thine eyes, and see what is this that goeth forth.

units.leftText: “What is it?” I asked. And he replied, “A measuring basket is going forth.” Then he continued, “This is their iniquity in all the land.”
units.rightText: And I said, What is it? And he said, This is the ephah that goeth forth. He said moreover, This is their appearance in all the land
leftNotes: 5:6 Or An ephah
5:6 One Hebrew manuscript, LXX, and Syriac; most Hebrew manuscripts their appearance or (literally) their eye

units.leftText: And behold, the cover of lead was raised, and there was a woman sitting inside the basket.
units.rightText: (and, behold, there was lifted up a talent of lead); and this is a woman sitting in the midst of the ephah.

units.leftText: “This is Wickedness,” he said. And he shoved her down into the basket, pushing down the lead cover over its opening.
units.rightText: And he said, This is Wickedness: and he cast her down into the midst of the ephah; and he cast the weight of lead upon the mouth thereof.

units.leftText: Then I lifted up my eyes and saw two women approaching, with the wind in their wings. Their wings were like those of a stork, and they lifted up the basket between heaven and earth.
units.rightText: Then lifted I up mine eyes, and saw, and, behold, there came forth two women, and the wind was in their wings; now they had wings like the wings of a stork; and they lifted up the ephah between earth and heaven.

units.leftText: “Where are they taking the basket?” I asked the angel who was speaking with me.
units.rightText: Then said I to the angel that talked with me, Whither do these bear the ephah?

units.leftText: “To build a house for it in the land of Shinar, ” he told me. “And when it is ready, the basket will be set there on its pedestal.”
units.rightText: And he said unto me, To build her a house in the land of Shinar: and when it is prepared, she shall be set there in her own place.
leftNotes: 5:11 That is, Babylonia

units.leftText: And again I lifted up my eyes and saw four chariots coming out from between two mountains — mountains of bronze.
units.rightText: And again I lifted up mine eyes, and saw, and, behold, there came four chariots out from between two mountains; and the mountains were mountains of brass.

units.leftText: The first chariot had red horses, the second black horses,
units.rightText: In the first chariot were red horses; and in the second chariot black horses;

units.leftText: the third white horses, and the fourth dappled horses— all of them strong.
units.rightText: and in the third chariot white horses; and in the fourth chariot grizzled strong horses.

units.leftText: So I inquired of the angel who was speaking with me, “What are these, my lord?”
units.rightText: Then I answered and said unto the angel that talked with me, What are these, my lord?

units.leftText: And the angel told me, “These are the four spirits of heaven, going forth from their station before the Lord of all the earth.
units.rightText: And the angel answered and said unto me, These are the four winds of heaven, which go forth from standing before the Lord of all the earth.
leftNotes: 6:5 Or winds

units.leftText: The one with the black horses is going toward the land of the north, the one with the white horses toward the west, and the one with the dappled horses toward the south.”
units.rightText: The chariot wherein are the black horses goeth forth toward the north country; and the white went forth after them; and the grizzled went forth toward the south country.
leftNotes: 6:6 Or the one with the white horses after them

units.leftText: As the strong horses went out, they were eager to go and patrol the earth; and the LORD said, “Go and patrol the earth.” So they patrolled the earth.
units.rightText: And the strong went forth, and sought to go that they might walk to and fro through the earth: and he said, Get you hence, walk to and fro through the earth. So they walked to and fro through the earth.

units.leftText: Then the LORD summoned me and said, “Behold, those going to the land of the north have given rest to My Spirit in the land of the north.” The Crown and the Temple
units.rightText: Then cried he to me, and spake unto me, saying, Behold, they that go toward the north country have quieted my spirit in the north country.

units.leftText: The word of the LORD also came to me, saying,
units.rightText: And the word of Jehovah came unto me, saying,

units.leftText: “Take an offering from the exiles — from Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah, who have arrived from Babylon — and go that same day to the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah.
units.rightText: Take of them of the captivity, even of Heldai, of Tobijah, and of Jedaiah; and come thou the same day, and go into the house of Josiah the son of Zephaniah, whither they are come from Babylon;

units.leftText: Take silver and gold, make an ornate crown, and set it on the head of the high priest, Joshua son of Jehozadak.
units.rightText: yea, take of them silver and gold, and make crowns, and set them upon the head of Joshua the son of Jehozadak, the high priest;
leftNotes: 6:11 Jehozadak is a variant of Jozadak; see Ezra 3:2|EZR 3:2*.

units.leftText: And you are to tell him that this is what the LORD of Hosts says: ‘Here is a man whose name is the Branch, and He will branch out from His place and build the temple of the LORD.
units.rightText: and speak unto him, saying, Thus speaketh Jehovah of hosts, saying, Behold, the man whose name is the Branch: and he shall grow up out of his place; and he shall build the temple of Jehovah;

units.leftText: Yes, He will build the temple of the LORD; He will be clothed in splendor and will sit on His throne and rule. And He will be a priest on His throne, and there will be peaceful counsel between the two.’
units.rightText: even he shall build the temple of Jehovah; and he shall bear the glory, and shall sit and rule upon his throne; and he shall be a priest upon his throne; and the counsel of peace shall be between them both.
leftNotes: 6:13 Or And there will be a priest on His throne

units.leftText: The crown will reside in the temple of the LORD as a memorial to Helem, Tobijah, Jedaiah, and the gracious son of Zephaniah.
units.rightText: And the crowns shall be to Helem, and to Tobijah, and to Jedaiah, and to Hen the son of Zephaniah, for a memorial in the temple of Jehovah.
leftNotes: 6:14 Hebrew; Syriac Heldai; see verse 10.
6:14 Or and Hen; Syriac and Josiah; see verse 10.

units.leftText: Even those far away will come and build the temple of the LORD, and you will know that the LORD of Hosts has sent Me to you. This will happen if you diligently obey the voice of the LORD your God.”
units.rightText: And they that are far off shall come and build in the temple of Jehovah; and ye shall know that Jehovah of hosts hath sent me unto you. And this shall come to pass, if ye will diligently obey the voice of Jehovah your God.

units.leftText: In the fourth year of King Darius, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah on the fourth day of the ninth month, the month of Chislev.
units.rightText: And it came to pass in the fourth year of king Darius, that the word of Jehovah came unto Zechariah in the fourth day of the ninth month, even in Chislev.
leftNotes: 7:1 Chislev is the ninth month of the Hebrew lunar calendar, usually occurring within the months of November and December.

units.leftText: Now the people of Bethel had sent Sharezer and Regem-melech, along with their men, to plead before the LORD
units.rightText: Now they of Beth-el had sent Sharezer and Regem-melech, and their men, to entreat the favor of Jehovah,
leftNotes: 7:2 Or Bethel-sharezer had sent Regem-melech, along with his men,

units.leftText: by asking the priests of the house of the LORD of Hosts, as well as the prophets, “Should I weep and fast in the fifth month, as I have done these many years?”
units.rightText: and to speak unto the priests of the house of Jehovah of hosts, and to the prophets, saying, Should I weep in the fifth month, separating myself, as I have done these so many years?

units.leftText: Then the word of the LORD of Hosts came to me, saying,
units.rightText: Then came the word of Jehovah of hosts unto me, saying,

units.leftText: “Ask all the people of the land and the priests, ‘When you fasted and mourned in the fifth and seventh months for these seventy years, was it really for Me that you fasted?
units.rightText: Speak unto all the people of the land, and to the priests, saying, When ye fasted and mourned in the fifth and in the seventh month, even these seventy years, did ye at all fast unto me, even to me?

units.leftText: And when you were eating and drinking, were you not doing so simply for yourselves?
units.rightText: And when ye eat, and when ye drink, do not ye eat for yourselves, and drink for yourselves?

units.leftText: Are these not the words that the LORD proclaimed through the earlier prophets, when Jerusalem and its surrounding towns were populous and prosperous, and the Negev and the foothills were inhabited?’”
units.rightText: Should ye not hear the words which Jehovah cried by the former prophets, when Jerusalem was inhabited and in prosperity, and the cities thereof round about her, and the South and the lowland were inhabited?
leftNotes: 7:7 Hebrew Shephelah or lowlands; that is, the western foothills of Judea

units.leftText: Then the word of the LORD came to Zechariah, saying,
units.rightText: And the word of Jehovah came unto Zechariah, saying,

units.leftText: “This is what the LORD of Hosts says: ‘Administer true justice. Show loving devotion and compassion to one another.
units.rightText: Thus hath Jehovah of hosts spoken, saying, Execute true judgment, and show kindness and compassion every man to his brother;
leftNotes: 7:9 Forms of the Hebrew chesed are translated here and in most cases throughout the Scriptures as loving devotion; the range of meaning includes love, goodness, kindness, faithfulness, and mercy, as well as loyalty to a covenant.

units.leftText: Do not oppress the widow or the fatherless, the foreigner or the poor. And do not plot evil in your hearts against one another.’
units.rightText: and oppress not the widow, nor the fatherless, the sojourner, nor the poor; and let none of you devise evil against his brother in your heart.

units.leftText: But they refused to pay attention and turned a stubborn shoulder; they stopped up their ears from hearing.
units.rightText: But they refused to hearken, and pulled away the shoulder, and stopped their ears, that they might not hear.
leftNotes: 7:11 Hebrew they made their ears too heavy to hear

units.leftText: They made their hearts like flint and would not listen to the law or to the words that the LORD of Hosts had sent by His Spirit through the earlier prophets. Therefore great anger came from the LORD of Hosts.
units.rightText: Yea, they made their hearts as an adamant stone, lest they should hear the law, and the words which Jehovah of hosts had sent by his Spirit by the former prophets: therefore there came great wrath from Jehovah of hosts.

units.leftText: And just as I had called and they would not listen, so when they called I would not listen, says the LORD of Hosts.
units.rightText: And it is come to pass that, as he cried, and they would not hear, so they shall cry, and I will not hear, said Jehovah of hosts;

units.leftText: But I scattered them with a whirlwind among all the nations that they had not known, and the land was left desolate behind them so that no one could come or go. Thus they turned the pleasant land into a desolation.”
units.rightText: but I will scatter them with a whirlwind among all the nations which they have not known. Thus the land was desolate after them, so that no man passed through nor returned: for they laid the pleasant land desolate.

units.leftText: Again the word of the LORD of Hosts came to me, saying:
units.rightText: And the word of Jehovah of hosts came to me, saying,

units.leftText: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: “I am jealous for Zion with great zeal; I am jealous for her with great fervor.”
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah of hosts: I am jealous for Zion with great jealousy, and I am jealous for her with great wrath.

units.leftText: This is what the LORD says: “I will return to Zion and dwell in Jerusalem. Then Jerusalem will be called the City of Truth, and the mountain of the LORD of Hosts will be called the Holy Mountain.”
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah: I am returned unto Zion, and will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem: and Jerusalem shall be called The city of truth; and the mountain of Jehovah of hosts, The holy mountain.

units.leftText: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Old men and old women will again sit along the streets of Jerusalem, each with a staff in hand because of great age.
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah of hosts: There shall yet old men and old women dwell in the streets of Jerusalem, every man with his staff in his hand for very age.

units.leftText: And the streets of the city will be filled with boys and girls playing there.”
units.rightText: And the streets of the city shall be full of boys and girls playing in the streets thereof.

units.leftText: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: “If this is impossible in the eyes of the remnant of this people in these days, should it also be impossible in My eyes?” declares the LORD of Hosts.
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah of hosts: If it be marvellous in the eyes of the remnant of this people in those days, should it also be marvellous in mine eyes? saith Jehovah of hosts.
leftNotes: 8:6 Or marvelous; twice in this verse

units.leftText: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: “I will save My people from the land of the east and from the land of the west.
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah of hosts: Behold, I will save my people from the east country, and from the west country;

units.leftText: I will bring them back to dwell in Jerusalem, where they will be My people, and I will be their faithful and righteous God.”
units.rightText: and I will bring them, and they shall dwell in the midst of Jerusalem; and they shall be my people, and I will be their God, in truth and in righteousness.

units.leftText: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Let your hands be strong, you who now hear these words spoken by the prophets who were present when the foundations were laid to rebuild the temple, the house of the LORD of Hosts.
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah of hosts: Let your hands be strong, ye that hear in these days these words from the mouth of the prophets that were in the day that the foundation of the house of Jehovah of hosts was laid, even the temple, that it might be built.

units.leftText: For before those days neither man nor beast received wages, nor was there safety from the enemy for anyone who came or went, for I had turned every man against his neighbor.
units.rightText: For before those days there was no hire for man, nor any hire for beast; neither was there any peace to him that went out or came in, because of the adversary: for I set all men every one against his neighbor.

units.leftText: But now I will not treat the remnant of this people as I did in the past,” declares the LORD of Hosts.
units.rightText: But now I will not be unto the remnant of this people as in the former days, saith Jehovah of hosts.

units.leftText: “For the seed will be prosperous, the vine will yield its fruit, the ground will yield its produce, and the skies will give their dew. To the remnant of this people I will give all these things as an inheritance.
units.rightText: For there shall be the seed of peace; the vine shall give its fruit, and the ground shall give its increase, and the heavens shall give their dew; and I will cause the remnant of this people to inherit all these things.

units.leftText: As you have been a curse among the nations, O house of Judah and house of Israel, so I will save you, and you will be a blessing. Do not be afraid; let your hands be strong.”
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass that, as ye were a curse among the nations, O house of Judah and house of Israel, so will I save you, and ye shall be a blessing. Fear not, but let your hands be strong.

units.leftText: For this is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Just as I resolved to bring disaster upon you when your fathers provoked Me to anger, and I did not relent,” says the LORD of Hosts,
units.rightText: For thus saith Jehovah of hosts: As I thought to do evil unto you, when your fathers provoked me to wrath, saith Jehovah of hosts, and I repented not;

units.leftText: “so now I have resolved to do good again to Jerusalem and Judah. Do not be afraid.
units.rightText: so again have I thought in these days to do good unto Jerusalem and to the house of Judah: fear ye not.

units.leftText: These are the things you must do: Speak truth to one another, render true and sound judgments in your gates,
units.rightText: These are the things that ye shall do: Speak ye every man the truth with his neighbor; execute the judgment of truth and peace in your gates;

units.leftText: do not plot evil in your hearts against your neighbor, and do not love to swear falsely, for I hate all these things,” declares the LORD.
units.rightText: and let none of you devise evil in your hearts against his neighbor; and love no false oath: for all these are things that I hate, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: Then the word of the LORD of Hosts came to me, saying,
units.rightText: And the word of Jehovah of hosts came unto me, saying,

units.leftText: “This is what the LORD of Hosts says: The fasts of the fourth, the fifth, the seventh, and the tenth months will become times of joy and gladness, cheerful feasts for the house of Judah. Therefore you are to love both truth and peace.”
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah of hosts: The fast of the fourth month, and the fast of the fifth, and the fast of the seventh, and the fast of the tenth, shall be to the house of Judah joy and gladness, and cheerful feasts; therefore love truth and peace.

units.leftText: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Peoples will yet come — the residents of many cities —
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah of hosts: It shall yet come to pass, that there shall come peoples, and the inhabitants of many cities;

units.leftText: and the residents of one city will go to another, saying: ‘Let us go at once to plead before the LORD and to seek the LORD of Hosts. I myself am going.’
units.rightText: and the inhabitants of one city shall go to another, saying, Let us go speedily to entreat the favor of Jehovah, and to seek Jehovah of hosts: I will go also.

units.leftText: And many peoples and strong nations will come to seek the LORD of Hosts in Jerusalem and to plead before the LORD.”
units.rightText: Yea, many peoples and strong nations shall come to seek Jehovah of hosts in Jerusalem, and to entreat the favor of Jehovah.

units.leftText: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: “In those days ten men from the nations of every tongue will tightly grasp the robe of a Jew, saying, ‘Let us go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.’”
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah of hosts: In those days it shall come to pass, that ten men shall take hold, out of all the languages of the nations, they shall take hold of the skirt of him that is a Jew, saying, We will go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.

units.leftText: This is the burden of the word of the LORD against the land of Hadrach and Damascus its resting place— for the eyes of men and of all the tribes of Israel are upon the LORD —
units.rightText: The burden of the word of Jehovah upon the land of Hadrach, and Damascus shall be its resting-place (for the eye of man and of all the tribes of Israel is toward Jehovah);
leftNotes: 9:1 Or for the eye of the LORD is on all men and all the tribes of Israel

units.leftText: and also against Hamath, which borders it, as well as Tyre and Sidon, though they are very shrewd.
units.rightText: and Hamath, also, which bordereth thereon; Tyre and Sidon, because they are very wise.

units.leftText: Tyre has built herself a fortress; she has heaped up silver like dust, and gold like the dirt of the streets.
units.rightText: And Tyre did build herself a stronghold, and heaped up silver as the dust, and fine gold as the mire of the streets.

units.leftText: Behold, the Lord will impoverish her and cast her wealth into the sea, and she will be consumed by fire.
units.rightText: Behold, the Lord will dispossess her, and he will smite her power in the sea; and she shall be devoured with fire.
leftNotes: 9:4 Or strike down her power on the sea

units.leftText: Ashkelon will see and fear; Gaza will writhe in agony, as will Ekron, for her hope will wither. There will cease to be a king in Gaza, and Ashkelon will be uninhabited.
units.rightText: Ashkelon shall see it, and fear; Gaza also, and shall be sore pained; and Ekron, for her expectation shall be put to shame; and the king shall perish from Gaza, and Ashkelon shall not be inhabited.

units.leftText: A mixed race will occupy Ashdod, and I will cut off the pride of the Philistines.
units.rightText: And a bastard shall dwell in Ashdod, and I will cut off the pride of the Philistines.

units.leftText: I will remove the blood from their mouths and the abominations from between their teeth. Then they too will become a remnant for our God; they will become like a clan in Judah, and Ekron will be like the Jebusites.
units.rightText: And I will take away his blood out of his mouth, and his abominations from between his teeth; and he also shall be a remnant for our God; and he shall be as a chieftain in Judah, and Ekron as a Jebusite.
leftNotes: 9:7 Or like a leader

units.leftText: But I will camp around My house because of an army, because of those who march to and fro, and never again will an oppressor overrun My people, for now I keep watch with My own eyes. Zion’s Coming King (Matthew 21:1–11|MAT 21:1-11*; Mark 11:1–11|MRK 11:1-11*; Luke 19:28–40|LUK 19:28-40*; John 12:12–19|JHN 12:12-19*)
units.rightText: And I will encamp about my house against the army, that none pass through or return; and no oppressor shall pass through them any more: for now have I seen with mine eyes.

units.leftText: Rejoice greatly, O Daughter of Zion! Shout in triumph, O Daughter of Jerusalem! See, your King comes to you, righteous and victorious, humble and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.
units.rightText: Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy king cometh unto thee; he is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass, even upon a colt the foal of an ass.
leftNotes: 9:9 Or righteous and endowed with salvation
9:9 Cited in Matthew 21:5|MAT 21:5* and John 12:15

units.leftText: And I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim and the horse from Jerusalem, and the bow of war will be broken. Then He will proclaim peace to the nations. His dominion will extend from sea to sea, and from the Euphrates to the ends of the earth.
units.rightText: And I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim, and the horse from Jerusalem; and the battle bow shall be cut off; and he shall speak peace unto the nations: and his dominion shall be from sea to sea, and from the River to the ends of the earth.
leftNotes: 9:10 That is, the northern kingdom of Israel
9:10 Hebrew the River

units.leftText: As for you, because of the blood of My covenant, I will release your prisoners from the waterless pit.
units.rightText: As for thee also, because of the blood of thy covenant I have set free thy prisoners from the pit wherein is no water.

units.leftText: Return to your stronghold, O prisoners of hope; even today I declare that I will restore to you double.
units.rightText: Turn you to the stronghold, ye prisoners of hope: even to-day do I declare that I will render double unto thee.

units.leftText: For I will bend Judah as My bow and fit it with Ephraim. I will rouse your sons, O Zion, against the sons of Greece. I will make you like the sword of a mighty man. The LORD Will Save His People
units.rightText: For I have bent Judah for me, I have filled the bow with Ephraim; and I will stir up thy sons, O Zion, against thy sons, O Greece, and will make thee as the sword of a mighty man.
leftNotes: 9:13 Hebrew the sons of Javan

units.leftText: Then the LORD will appear over them, and His arrow will go forth like lightning. The Lord GOD will sound the ram’s horn and advance in the whirlwinds of the south.
units.rightText: And Jehovah shall be seen over them; and his arrow shall go forth as the lightning; and the Lord Jehovah will blow the trumpet, and will go with whirlwinds of the south.

units.leftText: The LORD of Hosts will shield them. They will destroy and conquer with slingstones; they will drink and roar as with wine. And they will be filled like sprinkling bowls, drenched like the corners of the altar.
units.rightText: Jehovah of hosts will defend them; and they shall devour, and shall tread down the sling-stones; and they shall drink, and make a noise as through wine; and they shall be filled like bowls, like the corners of the altar.

units.leftText: On that day the LORD their God will save them as the flock of His people; for like jewels in a crown they will sparkle over His land.
units.rightText: And Jehovah their God will save them in that day as the flock of his people; for they shall be as the stones of a crown, lifted on high over his land.

units.leftText: How lovely they will be, and how beautiful! Grain will make the young men flourish, and new wine, the young women.
units.rightText: For how great is his goodness, and how great is his beauty! grain shall make the young men flourish, and new wine the virgins.

units.leftText: Ask the LORD for rain in springtime; the LORD makes the storm clouds, and He will give everyone showers of rain and crops in the field.
units.rightText: Ask ye of Jehovah rain in the time of the latter rain, even of Jehovah that maketh lightnings; and he will give them showers of rain, to every one grass in the field.

units.leftText: For idols speak deceit and diviners see illusions; they tell false dreams and offer empty comfort. Therefore the people wander like sheep, oppressed for lack of a shepherd.
units.rightText: For the teraphim have spoken vanity, and the diviners have seen a lie; and they have told false dreams, they comfort in vain: therefore they go their way like sheep, they are afflicted, because there is no shepherd.

units.leftText: “My anger burns against the shepherds, and I will punish the leaders. For the LORD of Hosts attends to His flock, the house of Judah; He will make them like His royal steed in battle.
units.rightText: Mine anger is kindled against the shepherds, and I will punish the he-goats; for Jehovah of hosts hath visited his flock, the house of Judah, and will make them as his goodly horse in the battle.
leftNotes: 10:3 Or these male goats

units.leftText: The cornerstone will come from Judah, the tent peg from him, as well as the battle bow and every ruler together.
units.rightText: From him shall come forth the corner-stone, from him the nail, from him the battle bow, from him every ruler together.

units.leftText: They will be like mighty men in battle, trampling the enemy in the mire of the streets. They will fight because the LORD is with them, and they will put the horsemen to shame.
units.rightText: And they shall be as mighty men, treading down their enemies in the mire of the streets in the battle; and they shall fight, because Jehovah is with them; and the riders on horses shall be confounded.

units.leftText: I will strengthen the house of Judah and save the house of Joseph. I will restore them because I have compassion on them, and they will be as though I had not rejected them. For I am the LORD their God, and I will answer them.
units.rightText: And I will strengthen the house of Judah, and I will save the house of Joseph, and I will bring them back; for I have mercy upon them; and they shall be as though I had not cast them off: for I am Jehovah their God, and I will hear them.

units.leftText: Ephraim will be like a mighty man, and their hearts will be glad as with wine. Their children will see it and be joyful; their hearts will rejoice in the LORD.
units.rightText: And they of Ephraim shall be like a mighty man, and their heart shall rejoice as through wine; yea, their children shall see it, and rejoice; their heart shall be glad in Jehovah.

units.leftText: I will whistle for them to gather, for I have redeemed them; and they will be as numerous as they once were.
units.rightText: I will hiss for them, and gather them; for I have redeemed them; and they shall increase as they have increased.

units.leftText: Though I sow them among the nations, they will remember Me in distant lands; they and their children will live and return.
units.rightText: And I will sow them among the peoples; and they shall remember me in far countries; and they shall live with their children, and shall return.

units.leftText: I will bring them back from Egypt and gather them from Assyria. I will bring them to Gilead and Lebanon until no more room is found for them.
units.rightText: I will bring them again also out of the land of Egypt, and gather them out of Assyria; and I will bring them into the land of Gilead and Lebanon; and place shall not be found for them.

units.leftText: They will pass through the sea of distress and strike the waves of the sea; all the depths of the Nile will dry up. The pride of Assyria will be brought down, and the scepter of Egypt will depart.
units.rightText: And he will pass through the sea of affliction, and will smite the waves in the sea, and all the depths of the Nile shall dry up; and the pride of Assyria shall be brought down, and the sceptre of Egypt shall depart.

units.leftText: I will strengthen them in the LORD, and in His name they will walk,” declares the LORD.
units.rightText: And I will strengthen them in Jehovah; and they shall walk up and down in his name, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: Open your doors, O Lebanon, that the fire may consume your cedars!
units.rightText: Open thy doors, O Lebanon, that the fire may devour thy cedars.

units.leftText: Wail, O cypress, for the cedar has fallen; the majestic trees are ruined! Wail, O oaks of Bashan, for the dense forest has been cut down!
units.rightText: Wail, O fir-tree, for the cedar is fallen, because the goodly ones are destroyed: wail, O ye oaks of Bashan, for the strong forest is come down.
leftNotes: 11:2 Or pine or juniper or fir

units.leftText: Listen to the wailing of the shepherds, for their glory is in ruins. Listen to the roaring of the young lions, for the thickets of the Jordan are destroyed.
units.rightText: A voice of the wailing of the shepherds! for their glory is destroyed: a voice of the roaring of young lions! for the pride of the Jordan is laid waste.

units.leftText: This is what the LORD my God says: “Pasture the flock marked for slaughter,
units.rightText: Thus said Jehovah my God: Feed the flock of slaughter;

units.leftText: whose buyers slaughter them without remorse. Those who sell them say, ‘Blessed be the LORD, for I am rich!’ Even their own shepherds have no compassion on them.
units.rightText: whose possessors slay them, and hold themselves not guilty; and they that sell them say, Blessed be Jehovah, for I am rich; and their own shepherds pity them not.

units.leftText: For I will no longer have compassion on the people of the land, declares the LORD, but behold, I will cause each man to fall into the hands of his neighbor and his king, who will devastate the land, and I will not deliver it from their hands.”
units.rightText: For I will no more pity the inhabitants of the land, saith Jehovah; but, lo, I will deliver the men every one into his neighbor’s hand, and into the hand of his king; and they shall smite the land, and out of their hand I will not deliver them.

units.leftText: So I pastured the flock marked for slaughter, especially the afflicted of the flock. Then I took for myself two staffs, calling one Favor and the other Union, and I pastured the flock.
units.rightText: So I fed the flock of slaughter, verily the poor of the flock. And I took unto me two staves; the one I called Beauty, and the other I called Bands; and I fed the flock.

units.leftText: And in one month I dismissed three shepherds.
units.rightText: And I cut off the three shepherds in one month; for my soul was weary of them, and their soul also loathed me.

units.leftText: Then I said, “I will no longer shepherd you. Let the dying die, and the perishing perish; and let those who remain devour one another’s flesh.” Thirty Pieces of Silver (Matthew 27:3–10|MAT 27:3-10*)
units.rightText: Then said I, I will not feed you: that which dieth, let it die; and that which is to be cut off, let it be cut off; and let them that are left eat every one the flesh of another.

units.leftText: Next I took my staff called Favor and cut it in two, revoking the covenant I had made with all the nations.
units.rightText: And I took my staff Beauty, and cut it asunder, that I might break my covenant which I had made with all the peoples.
leftNotes: 11:10 Or broke it; similarly in verse 14

units.leftText: It was revoked on that day, and so the afflicted of the flock who were watching me knew that it was the word of the LORD.
units.rightText: And it was broken in that day; and thus the poor of the flock that gave heed unto me knew that it was the word of Jehovah.

units.leftText: Then I told them, “If it seems right to you, give me my wages; but if not, keep them.” So they weighed out my wages, thirty pieces of silver.
units.rightText: And I said unto them, If ye think good, give me my hire; and if not, forbear. So they weighed for my hire thirty pieces of silver.

units.leftText: And the LORD said to me, “Throw it to the potter”— this magnificent price at which they valued me. So I took the thirty pieces of silver and threw them to the potter in the house of the LORD.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto me, Cast it unto the potter, the goodly price that I was prized at by them. And I took the thirty pieces of silver, and cast them unto the potter, in the house of Jehovah.

units.leftText: Then I cut in two my second staff called Union, breaking the brotherhood between Judah and Israel.
units.rightText: Then I cut asunder mine other staff, even Bands, that I might break the brotherhood between Judah and Israel.

units.leftText: And the LORD said to me: “Take up once more the equipment of a foolish shepherd.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto me, Take unto thee yet again the instruments of a foolish shepherd.

units.leftText: For behold, I will raise up a shepherd in the land who will neither care for the lost, nor seek the young, nor heal the broken, nor sustain the healthy, but he will devour the flesh of the choice sheep and tear off their hooves.
units.rightText: For, lo, I will raise up a shepherd in the land, who will not visit those that are cut off, neither will seek those that are scattered, nor heal that which is broken, nor feed that which is sound; but he will eat the flesh of the fat sheep, and will tear their hoofs in pieces.

units.leftText: Woe to the worthless shepherd, who deserts the flock! May a sword strike his arm and his right eye! May his arm be completely withered and his right eye utterly blinded!”
units.rightText: Woe to the worthless shepherd that leaveth the flock! the sword shall be upon his arm, and upon his right eye: his arm shall be clean dried up, and his right eye shall be utterly darkened.

units.leftText: This is the burden of the word of the LORD concerning Israel. Thus declares the LORD, who stretches out the heavens and lays the foundation of the earth, who forms the spirit of man within him:
units.rightText: The burden of the word of Jehovah concerning Israel. Thus saith Jehovah, who stretcheth forth the heavens, and layeth the foundation of the earth, and formeth the spirit of man within him:

units.leftText: “Behold, I will make Jerusalem a cup of drunkenness to all the surrounding peoples. Judah will be besieged, as well as Jerusalem.
units.rightText: Behold, I will make Jerusalem a cup of reeling unto all the peoples round about, and upon Judah also shall it be in the siege against Jerusalem.

units.leftText: On that day, when all the nations of the earth gather against her, I will make Jerusalem a heavy stone for all the peoples; all who would heave it away will be severely injured.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass in that day, that I will make Jerusalem a burdensome stone for all the peoples; all that burden themselves with it shall be sore wounded; and all the nations of the earth shall be gathered together against it.

units.leftText: On that day, declares the LORD, I will strike every horse with panic, and every rider with madness. I will keep a watchful eye on the house of Judah, but I will strike with blindness all the horses of the nations.
units.rightText: In that day, saith Jehovah, I will smite every horse with terror, and his rider with madness; and I will open mine eyes upon the house of Judah, and will smite every horse of the peoples with blindness.

units.leftText: Then the leaders of Judah will say in their hearts: ‘The people of Jerusalem are my strength, for the LORD of Hosts is their God.’
units.rightText: And the chieftains of Judah shall say in their heart, The inhabitants of Jerusalem are my strength in Jehovah of hosts their God.

units.leftText: On that day I will make the clans of Judah like a firepot in a woodpile, like a flaming torch among the sheaves; they will consume all the peoples around them on the right and on the left, while the people of Jerusalem remain secure there.
units.rightText: In that day will I make the chieftains of Judah like a pan of fire among wood, and like a flaming torch among sheaves; and they shall devour all the peoples round about, on the right hand and on the left; and they of Jerusalem shall yet again dwell in their own place, even in Jerusalem.

units.leftText: The LORD will save the tents of Judah first, so that the glory of the house of David and of the people of Jerusalem may not be greater than that of Judah.
units.rightText: Jehovah also shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem be not magnified above Judah.

units.leftText: On that day the LORD will defend the people of Jerusalem, so that the weakest among them will be like David, and the house of David will be like God, like the angel of the LORD going before them.
units.rightText: In that day shall Jehovah defend the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and he that is feeble among them at that day shall be as David; and the house of David shall be as God, as the angel of Jehovah before them.
leftNotes: 12:8 Or Angel

units.leftText: So on that day I will set out to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem. Mourning the One They Pierced (John 19:31–37|JHN 19:31-37*)
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass in that day, that I will seek to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Then I will pour out on the house of David and on the people of Jerusalem a spirit of grace and prayer, and they will look on Me, the One they have pierced. They will mourn for Him as one mourns for an only child, and grieve bitterly for Him as one grieves for a firstborn son.
units.rightText: And I will pour upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and of supplication; and they shall look unto me whom they have pierced; and they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son, and shall be in bitterness for him, as one that is in bitterness for his first-born.
leftNotes: 12:10 Or the Spirit
12:10 Or to Me
12:10 Cited in John 19:37|JHN 19:37*

units.leftText: On that day the wailing in Jerusalem will be as great as the wailing of Hadad-rimmon in the plain of Megiddo.
units.rightText: In that day shall there be a great mourning in Jerusalem, as the mourning of Hadadrimmon in the valley of Megiddon.

units.leftText: The land will mourn, each clan on its own: the clan of the house of David and their wives, the clan of the house of Nathan and their wives,
units.rightText: And the land shall mourn, every family apart; the family of the house of David apart, and their wives apart; the family of the house of Nathan apart, and their wives apart;

units.leftText: the clan of the house of Levi and their wives, the clan of Shimei and their wives,
units.rightText: the family of the house of Levi apart, and their wives apart; the family of the Shimeites apart, and their wives apart;

units.leftText: and all the remaining clans and their wives.[’’]
units.rightText: all the families that remain, every family apart, and their wives apart.

units.leftText: “On that day a fountain will be opened to the house of David and the people of Jerusalem, to cleanse them from sin and impurity.
units.rightText: In that day there shall be a fountain opened to the house of David and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, for sin and for uncleanness.

units.leftText: And on that day, declares the LORD of Hosts, I will erase the names of the idols from the land, and they will no longer be remembered. I will also remove the prophets and the spirit of impurity from the land.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass in that day, saith Jehovah of hosts, that I will cut off the names of the idols out of the land, and they shall no more be remembered; and also I will cause the prophets and the unclean spirit to pass out of the land.
leftNotes: 13:2 Or the unclean spirit

units.leftText: And if anyone still prophesies, his father and mother who bore him will say to him, ‘You shall not remain alive, because you have spoken falsely in the name of the LORD.’ When he prophesies, his father and mother who bore him will pierce him through.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass that, when any shall yet prophesy, then his father and his mother that begat him shall say unto him, Thou shalt not live; for thou speakest lies in the name of Jehovah; and his father and his mother that begat him shall thrust him through when he prophesieth.

units.leftText: And on that day every prophet who prophesies will be ashamed of his vision, and he will not put on a hairy cloak in order to deceive.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass in that day, that the prophets shall be ashamed every one of his vision, when he prophesieth; neither shall they wear a hairy mantle to deceive:

units.leftText: He will say, ‘I am not a prophet; I work the land, for I was purchased as a servant in my youth. ’
units.rightText: but he shall say, I am no prophet, I am a tiller of the ground; for I have been made a bondman from my youth.
leftNotes: 13:5 Or I am a farmer, for the land has been my livelihood since my youth.

units.leftText: If someone asks him, ‘What are these wounds on your chest ?’ he will answer, ‘These are the wounds I received in the house of my friends.’ The Shepherd Struck, the Sheep Scattered (Matthew 26:31–35|MAT 26:31-35*; Mark 14:27–31|MRK 14:27-31*)
units.rightText: And one shall say unto him, What are these wounds between thine arms? Then he shall answer, Those with which I was wounded in the house of my friends.
leftNotes: 13:6 Literally between your hands

units.leftText: Awake, O sword, against My Shepherd, against the man who is My Companion, declares the LORD of Hosts. Strike the Shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered, and I will turn My hand against the little ones.
units.rightText: Awake, O sword, against my shepherd, and against the man that is my fellow, saith Jehovah of hosts: smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered; and I will turn my hand upon the little ones.
leftNotes: 13:7 Cited in Matthew 26:31|MAT 26:31* and Mark 14:27

units.leftText: And in all the land, declares the LORD, two-thirds will be cut off and perish, but a third will be left in it.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass, that in all the land, saith Jehovah, two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein.

units.leftText: This third I will bring through the fire; I will refine them like silver and test them like gold. They will call on My name, and I will answer them. I will say, ‘They are My people,’ and they will say, ‘The LORD is our God.’”
units.rightText: And I will bring the third part into the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will try them as gold is tried. They shall call on my name, and I will hear them: I will say, It is my people; and they shall say, Jehovah is my God.

units.leftText: Behold, a day of the LORD is coming when your plunder will be divided in your presence.
units.rightText: Behold, a day of Jehovah cometh, when thy spoil shall be divided in the midst of thee.

units.leftText: For I will gather all the nations for battle against Jerusalem, and the city will be captured, the houses looted, and the women ravished. Half of the city will go into exile, but the rest of the people will not be removed from the city.
units.rightText: For I will gather all nations against Jerusalem to battle; and the city shall be taken, and the houses rifled, and the women ravished; and half of the city shall go forth into captivity, and the residue of the people shall not be cut off from the city.

units.leftText: Then the LORD will go out to fight against those nations, as He fights in the day of battle.
units.rightText: Then shall Jehovah go forth, and fight against those nations, as when he fought in the day of battle.

units.leftText: On that day His feet will stand on the Mount of Olives, east of Jerusalem, and the Mount of Olives will be split in two from east to west, forming a great valley, with half the mountain moving to the north and half to the south.
units.rightText: And his feet shall stand in that day upon the mount of Olives, which is before Jerusalem on the east; and the mount of Olives shall be cleft in the midst thereof toward the east and toward the west, and there shall be a very great valley; and half of the mountain shall remove toward the north, and half of it toward the south.

units.leftText: You will flee by My mountain valley, for it will extend to Azal. You will flee as you fled from the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah. Then the LORD my God will come, and all the holy ones with Him.
units.rightText: And ye shall flee by the valley of my mountains; for the valley of the mountains shall reach unto Azel; yea, ye shall flee, like as ye fled from before the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah; and Jehovah my God shall come, and all the holy ones with thee.
leftNotes: 14:5 LXX; Hebrew with You

units.leftText: On that day there will be no light, no cold or frost.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass in that day, that there shall not be light; the bright ones shall withdraw themselves:

units.leftText: It will be a unique day known only to the LORD, without day or night; but when evening comes, there will be light.
units.rightText: but it shall be one day which is known unto Jehovah; not day, and not night; but it shall come to pass, that at evening time there shall be light.

units.leftText: And on that day living water will flow out from Jerusalem, half of it toward the Eastern Sea and the other half toward the Western Sea, in summer and winter alike.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass in that day, that living waters shall go out from Jerusalem; half of them toward the eastern sea, and half of them toward the western sea: in summer and in winter shall it be.
leftNotes: 14:8 That is, the Dead Sea
14:8 That is, the Mediterranean Sea, also called the Great Sea

units.leftText: On that day the LORD will become King over all the earth— the LORD alone, and His name alone.
units.rightText: And Jehovah shall be King over all the earth: in that day shall Jehovah be one, and his name one.

units.leftText: All the land from Geba to Rimmon south of Jerusalem will be turned into a plain, but Jerusalem will be raised up and will remain in her place, from the Benjamin Gate to the site of the First Gate to the Corner Gate, and from the Tower of Hananel to the royal winepresses.
units.rightText: All the land shall be made like the Arabah, from Geba to Rimmon south of Jerusalem; and she shall be lifted up, and shall dwell in her place, from Benjamin’s gate unto the place of the first gate, unto the corner gate, and from the tower of Hananel unto the king’s winepresses.

units.leftText: People will live there, and never again will there be an utter destruction. So Jerusalem will dwell securely.
units.rightText: And men shall dwell therein, and there shall be no more curse; but Jerusalem shall dwell safely.

units.leftText: And this will be the plague with which the LORD strikes all the peoples who have warred against Jerusalem: Their flesh will rot while they stand on their feet, their eyes will rot in their sockets, and their tongues will rot in their mouths.
units.rightText: And this shall be the plague wherewith Jehovah will smite all the peoples that have warred against Jerusalem: their flesh shall consume away while they stand upon their feet, and their eyes shall consume away in their sockets, and their tongue shall consume away in their mouth.

units.leftText: On that day a great panic from the LORD will come upon them, so that each will seize the hand of another, and the hand of one will rise against the other.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass in that day, that a great tumult from Jehovah shall be among them; and they shall lay hold every one on the hand of his neighbor, and his hand shall rise up against the hand of his neighbor.

units.leftText: Judah will also fight at Jerusalem, and the wealth of all the surrounding nations will be collected — gold, silver, and apparel in great abundance.
units.rightText: And Judah also shall fight at Jerusalem; and the wealth of all the nations round about shall be gathered together, gold, and silver, and apparel, in great abundance.

units.leftText: And a similar plague will strike the horses and mules, camels and donkeys, and all the animals in those camps. All Nations Will Worship the King (Leviticus 23:33–44|LEV 23:33-44*; Nehemiah 8:13–18|NEH 8:13-18*)
units.rightText: And so shall be the plague of the horse, of the mule, of the camel, and of the ass, and of all the beasts that shall be in those camps, as that plague.

units.leftText: Then all the survivors from the nations that came against Jerusalem will go up year after year to worship the King, the LORD of Hosts, and to celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass, that every one that is left of all the nations that came against Jerusalem shall go up from year to year to worship the King, Jehovah of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles.
leftNotes: 14:16 That is, Sukkot, the autumn feast of pilgrimage to Jerusalem; also translated as the Feast of Booths or the Feast of Shelters and originally called the Feast of Ingathering(see Exodus 23:16|EXO 23:16* and Exodus 34:22).

units.leftText: And should any of the families of the earth not go up to Jerusalem to worship the King, the LORD of Hosts, then the rain will not fall on them.
units.rightText: And it shall be, that whoso of all the families of the earth goeth not up unto Jerusalem to worship the King, Jehovah of hosts, upon them there shall be no rain.

units.leftText: And if the people of Egypt will not go up and enter in, then the rain will not fall on them; this will be the plague with which the LORD strikes the nations who do not go up to celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles.
units.rightText: And if the family of Egypt go not up, and come not, neither shall it be upon them; there shall be the plague wherewith Jehovah will smite the nations that go not up to keep the feast of tabernacles.

units.leftText: This will be the punishment of Egypt and of all the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles.
units.rightText: This shall be the punishment of Egypt, and the punishment of all the nations that go not up to keep the feast of tabernacles.

units.leftText: On that day, HOLY TO THE LORD will be inscribed on the bells of the horses, and the cooking pots in the house of the LORD will be like the sprinkling bowls before the altar.
units.rightText: In that day shall there be upon the bells of the horses, HOLY UNTO JEHOVAH; and the pots in Jehovah’s house shall be like the bowls before the altar.
leftNotes: 14:20 That is, the LORD

units.leftText: Indeed, every pot in Jerusalem and Judah will be holy to the LORD of Hosts, and all who sacrifice will come and take some pots and cook in them. And on that day there will no longer be a Canaanite in the house of the LORD of Hosts.
units.rightText: Yea, every pot in Jerusalem and in Judah shall be holy unto Jehovah of hosts; and all they that sacrifice shall come and take of them, and boil therein: and in that day there shall be no more a Canaanite in the house of Jehovah of hosts.
leftNotes: 14:21 Or merchant
